subject: Matemática
description_pt: Resolver e elaborar problemas relacionados ao seu contexto próximo, que possam ser representados por sistemas de equações de 1º grau com duas incógnitas e interpretá-los, utilizando, inclusive, o plano cartesiano como recurso.

components.description_pt: Criar sistema de equações lineares em contexto do mundo real, incluindo representação de restrições
components.description_en: Create a system of linear equations in a real-world context, including representing constraints in the context
components.cc_component_description: Create a system of linear equations in a real-world context, including representing constraints in the context

components.description_pt: Resolver sistemas de equações lineares algebricamente
components.description_en: Solve systems of linear equations algebraically
components.cc_component_description: Solve systems of linear equations algebraically

components.description_pt: Interpretar a solução de um sistema de equações de primeiro grau em contexto de problema real
components.description_en: Interpret the solution of a system of first-degree equations in the context of a real-world problem
components.cc_component_description: Interpret the solution(s) to the equation f(x) = g(x) in context

components.description_pt: Usar o plano cartesiano para representar e resolver um sistema de duas equações de primeiro grau em duas incógnitas
components.description_en: Use the Cartesian plane to represent and solve a system of two first-degree equations in two unknowns
components.cc_component_description: Graph linear equations in two variables on a coordinate plane and label the axes and scales

cc_matches.description: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection. *For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.*

Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context. *For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.*

Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.
Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
